# pi-tools effort workflow

Use when durable continuity materially helps multi-step work, likely resumption, coordination, delegation, or preservation of settled decisions and observations. It is optional otherwise. This skill alone owns the effort resident and lifecycle; one user-managed writer updates its memory.

<!-- awf:edit continuity-and-resident: default; create .awf/skills/parts/effort-workflow/continuity-and-resident.md to override -->
## Continuity, identity, and resident

Judge continuity at entry and again when continuity-relevant facts change. Create or resume only when it helps. An effort has a fixed title and slug, one resident at `.awf/efforts/<slug>/memory.md`, and one deterministic managed worktree at `.awf/worktrees/<slug>` on `awf/<slug>`. Do not retitle, create parallel residents or worktrees, infer another topology, or use activity as a lock.

Create with the ordinary `./awf effort` creation command. If discussion predates creation, initialize the resident from retained evidence: outcome, settled decisions with actual approval evidence, observations, phase, and next action. Do not reconstruct missing approval evidence. On resume or takeover, validate the slug and resident path, identify the sole writer, and revalidate all checkpoint claims against repository authority, source, tests, history, and applicable current state. Memory is a checkpoint, not authority.

<!-- awf:edit execution-and-checkpoints: default; create .awf/skills/parts/effort-workflow/execution-and-checkpoints.md to override -->
## Execution, checkpoints, and handoff

Use the exact managed worktree for pre-integration work. Write a checkpoint at a meaningful resumable boundary: completed work, decisions and observations, verification, repository state, next action, and blockers. A handoff or switch requires such a checkpoint; the successor reorients and revalidates before substantive work. Before switching away, leave the current effort resumable or deliberately discontinue it after transferring necessary valid context.

A changed material outcome needs a fixed-identity successor, not a renamed effort. Create and make the successor resumable, transfer only valid context, then close the obsolete effort safely.

<!-- awf:edit integration-and-recovery: default; create .awf/skills/parts/effort-workflow/integration-and-recovery.md to override -->
## Integration, divergence, and recovery

After implementation and any risk-based review settle, reconcile material deviations in the resident. From the intended clean primary checkout, run `./awf effort integrate <slug>`. Integration is distinct from review, removal, and finish. If it is already integrated or fast-forwarded, confirm assurance still covers the resulting tip. If it diverges, resolve conflicts visibly, verify the combined result with the applicable checks, and obtain renewed risk-based review before removal.

Inspect identity and worktree state before recovery. Preserve unrelated work; do not use blind reset, restore, clean, or stash. Use native Git safety primitives explicitly only when intentionally discarding inspected obsolete work is necessary. Record the recovery and its consequence in the checkpoint.

<!-- awf:edit close: default; create .awf/skills/parts/effort-workflow/close.md to override -->
## Close last

When integrated assurance is settled, remove the managed worktree safely with `./awf effort worktree remove <slug>` without force and verify the path, registration, and branch are absent. Fold a retrospective into closure only when observations contain a reusable lesson; record that lesson where the project keeps durable lessons. Then run `./awf effort finish <slug>` last. It archives the complete resident; inspect source and destination after any uncertain result rather than blindly retrying. Never remove topology before integration and divergence assurance are complete.
